summary: In 1910 neighbours petitioned the Board against a laundry a man named Mori wanted to open on Sutter Street. In the 1950s and 60s the city widened Geary and Webster through here — its own engineers called Webster the first stage of a thoroughfare running through the heart of the Western Addition redevelopment area. Buchanan Street was closed to traffic in 1974, and the neighbourhood has been closing Post Street for the Obon dance and the Nihonmachi Street Fair almost every summer since. In 1997, and again in 2001, the Board took the side of the Soko Bukai in its claim on the YWCA building at 1830 Sutter Street.
